# Copilot / AI assistant instructions for Docitai repository

Quick reference to get productive in this monorepo. Keep answers short and prefer concrete edits over high-level advice.

- Repo layout: top-level `apps/`, `libs/`, `infra/`, `specs/`, `templates/`, `scripts/`, `memory/`.
- Design workflow: Spec-Driven Development. New features live under `specs/###-slug/` and are bootstrapped by scripts in `scripts/`.

Essential commands you can call (from repo root):
- `./setup.sh` — install deps + git hooks (developer setup).
- `scripts/create-new-feature.sh --json "{...}"` — create a new feature branch and initialized spec file; returns JSON with `BRANCH_NAME` and `SPEC_FILE`.
- `bash scripts/setup-plan.sh --json "{...}"` — initialize plan artifacts (returns `FEATURE_SPEC`, `IMPL_PLAN`, `SPECS_DIR`, `BRANCH`).
- `scripts/update-agent-context.sh` — adds/updates AI agent context files; use when updating assistant prompts or tech summary.

Where to look first (high value files):
- `memory/constitution.md` — canonical project constraints and tech stack (NestJS, Prisma, Postgres, OpenFGA, API-first). Respect this when proposing architecture.
- `templates/spec-template.md` — the spec shape and mandatory sections. When generating specs, preserve headings and mark missing items with `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: ...]`.
- `templates/plan-template.md` and `templates/tasks-template.md` — how planning and task generation should be structured.
- `scripts/create-new-feature.sh`, `scripts/setup-plan.sh`, `scripts/get-feature-paths.sh` — examples of repo automation and how features are wired into the specs folder.

Project-specific conventions and expectations:
- Spec-first, not implementation-first: produce or update `specs/<num>-slug/spec.md` following `spec-template.md` exactly (keep heading order).
- Use the repo scripts to create branches/specs so naming and paths are consistent (features are numbered `###`).
- Mark all ambiguities explicitly with `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: ...]` in specs — the plan flow treats those as blockers.
- Contracts and APIs are source-of-truth: generate OpenAPI under `specs/<feature>/contracts/` when designing APIs.

Integration points & infra expectations:
- Object storage (S3/GCS/Azure) is treated as external; specs must note whether provisioning is expected or external bucket identifiers will be supplied.
- Persistence: metadata in Postgres (Prisma), documents in object storage — mention these when defining the data-model and migration tasks.
- Authorization: system uses relationship-based model (OpenFGA). Design APIs and entities with tenant-scoped ids and an explicit `tenant_id` on tenant-bound resources.

How to author autogenerated artifacts and tests:
- Phase 0 (research): create `research.md` in the feature specs folder capturing decisions and open questions.
- Phase 1 (design): produce `data-model.md`, `contracts/openapi.yaml`, and `quickstart.md` in the same specs folder.
- Follow contract-first TDD: generate failing contract tests (schema assertions) before implementing endpoints. Place test stubs near services (or in a `tests/` folder) and reference the OpenAPI file.

Examples from this repo:
- When you run `scripts/create-new-feature.sh` it will create `/home/solmon/github/docitai/specs/002-title-tenant-management/spec.md` — use that path to update the spec.
- `templates/spec-template.md` requires `User Scenarios & Testing`, `Functional Requirements`, and `Key Entities` — fill these sections and preserve note markers.

What *not* to change automatically:
- Do not edit `memory/constitution.md` to satisfy a plan; instead document deviations in the plan's Complexity Tracking section.
- Avoid making implementation choices in specs (no tech stack, no code-level APIs) — those belong in Phase 1 design artifacts.

If uncertain, ask the user one specific question (not open-ended). Examples:
- "Should tenant onboarding allow automatic bucket provisioning, or accept existing bucket ARNs?"
- "What default retention durations (in days) should apply to 'invoices' and 'contracts'?"

After making edits
- Run `scripts/update-agent-context.sh` to refresh agent context files.
- Open a concise PR that includes the spec, plan, and contract artifacts with a short PR description linking to the feature spec.

If you want me to iterate on these instructions, tell me which sections need more or fewer details and whether to include command snippets for local testing.

End of instructions
